format:

    geometry: margin=1.25in
    fontsize: 11pt

```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = FALSE, warning = FALSE, message = FALSE)
library(here)
library(tidyverse)
here::i_am("errata.qmd")

# Entry 1's corrected count is read from the maintained pipeline's output rather than
# typed here: table_1_experiment_directory.R takes the union of the respondent identifiers
# in the ten deposited analysis files and writes it as the last row of Table 1.
table_1 <- read_csv(here("maintained", "output", "table_1_experiment_directory.csv"),
                    show_col_types = FALSE)
n_any <- table_1$n_deposited[table_1$experiment == "Any of the ten experiments"]
stopifnot(length(n_any) == 1, n_any > 85191)
n_ten_rows <- sum(table_1$n_deposited[table_1$experiment != "Any of the ten experiments"])

# Entry 2's counts are the number of distinct respondent identifiers in the deposited
# analysis files from each of waves five to eight, measured on 2026-10-31 and recorded
# here because the deposit is downloaded rather than committed. When the deposit is
# present the chunk recounts and refuses to render if the figures have moved.
wave_counts <- tribble(
  ~wave, ~largest_file,           ~n_largest, ~n_union, ~n_consort,
  5,     "data_w5_masking",        14557,      14557,    14557,
  6,     "data_w6_conversation",   30857,      30857,    30857,
  7,     "data_w7_cdcmask",        32943,      32989,    33088,
  8,     "data_w8_bivalent_all",   29448,      29448,    29448
)
data_dir <- here("original", "replication_archive", "data", "clean", "rds")
if (dir.exists(data_dir)) {
  recount <- tibble(file = list.files(data_dir, pattern = "^data_w[5-8]_.*[.]rds$")) |>
    mutate(wave = as.numeric(str_extract(file, "(?<=^data_w)\\d")),
           ids = map(file, function(f) read_rds(file.path(data_dir, f))$respondent_id)) |>
    group_by(wave) |>
    summarise(n_largest = max(lengths(ids)), n_union = length(reduce(ids, union)), .groups = "drop")
  stopifnot(nrow(recount) == nrow(wave_counts),
            all(recount$wave == wave_counts$wave),
            all(recount$n_largest == wave_counts$n_largest),
            all(recount$n_union == wave_counts$n_union))
}

# Entry 22's counts and p-values are read from the maintained replication, which uses the
# corrected standard error, and the chunk refuses to render if the counts move. The
# deposited-standard-error columns are kept in the same file.
equiv <- read_csv(here("maintained", "output", "text_equivalence_claims.csv"), show_col_types = FALSE)
vignettes <- filter(equiv, family == "Mandate vignette")
n_vig <- nrow(vignettes)
n_aff <- sum(vignettes$affirms_10pp)
stopifnot(n_vig == 4, n_aff == 1, sum(vignettes$affirms_10pp_deposited) == 2,
          vignettes$affirms_10pp[vignettes$experiment == "G-2 restaurant"],
          !vignettes$affirms_10pp[vignettes$experiment == "G-2 concert"],
          all(equiv$affirms_5pp == equiv$affirms_5pp_deposited),
          sum(equiv$affirms_10pp != equiv$affirms_10pp_deposited) == 1)
p10 <- function(x) sprintf("%.3f", vignettes$eq_p_10pp[vignettes$experiment == x])

# Entry 8's shares are the maintained replication's weighted means in the E-2 file.
endorse <- read_csv(here("maintained", "output", "text_endorsement_claims.csv"), show_col_types = FALSE)
share <- function(label) sprintf("%.1f", 100 * endorse$value[endorse$claim == label])
# Entry 47's corrected row values, formatted as the appendix prints them.
cell <- function(id, est, se) {
  r <- equiv[equiv$experiment == id, ]
  sprintf("%.3f (%.3f)%s", r[[est]], r[[se]], if (abs(r[[est]] / r[[se]]) > 1.96) " *" else "")
}
pstar <- function(id, p) {
  v <- equiv[[p]][equiv$experiment == id]
  sprintf("%.3f%s", v, if (v < 0.05) " *" else "")
}
fmt <- function(x) format(x, big.mark = ",")

# Numerals above ten are printed as numerals.
spell <- function(n) {
  words <- c("one", "two", "three", "four", "five", "six", "seven", "eight", "nine", "ten")
  stopifnot(n >= 1)
  if (n <= length(words)) words[n] else as.character(n)
}
```

```{r entries}
# THE ERRATA SPINE. Every entry is defined once, here, and rendered from here: into this
# document, and into whatever else needs it, which reads the errata_entries.csv written at
# the bottom of this file rather than keeping a second hand-typed copy.
#
# [[...]] marks the span that changes. Each renderer supplies its own markup for it: bold
# here, \was{} in an edition. Nothing else in a field is markup, so the same string can be
# set by either.
#
# Numbering is APPEND-ONLY once this note is published: an entry can already have been
# cited, so a later finding is added at the end and never interleaved.
#
# claim_ids names the ground-truth rows an entry corrects, semicolon-separated.
# corrected_values runs parallel to claim_ids, one value per id in the same order, on the
# claim's scale, carrying the corrected quantity as a number rather than as a sentence. Each
# value is computed once, here, and the corrected sentence below is glued from the same
# object, so the two cannot be written apart; the gate after the spine re-checks that each
# value sits inside the [[...]] span it belongs to. An entry of a class that changes no
# quantity, a note-form entry, and an entry with no claim_ids carry NA.
cv1 <- n_any
cv22 <- n_aff

entries <- tribble(
  ~entry, ~class, ~source, ~form, ~title, ~location, ~published, ~corrected, ~note, ~claim_ids, ~corrected_values,

  paste0("Using data from 10 experiments with [[", fmt(cv1), "]] survey respondents conducted over a 2-year period during the COVID-19 pandemic, we assess the effectiveness of these three types of persuasive messages."),

         "files, one per experiment in Table 1, hold ", fmt(n_ten_rows), " rows and ", fmt(n_any),
         " distinct respondent identifiers. Every identifier carries its wave as a prefix and no identifier ",
         "appears in two waves, so the overlap is entirely within waves, whose experiments draw on the same ",
         "respondents: the mandate vignettes and the first mask-guidance experiment share wave six, the two ",
         "conversation experiments and the second mask-guidance experiment share wave seven, and the three ",
         "booster experiments share wave eight. The analysis files run ",
         "0.1 to 0.7 percent short of the enrollment Table 1 reports, so the count of enrolled respondents is ",
         "larger still: Table 1's own N column, with the nested experiments counted once as the appendix's ",
         "CONSORT diagrams show them, gives at least 96,840. No sum of the N figures the article prints ",
         "produces 85,191, and the deposit contains no file from which it could have been counted. The ",
         "figure given here is the deposit's."),
  "abstract_and_introduction_survey_respondents_across_the_ten_experiments",
  as.character(cv1),

  paste0("The deposit ships experiment subsets rather than waves, but three of its wave-five files ",

         sprintf("%.3f", equiv$eq_p_10pp[equiv$experiment == "I-1"]), " when corrected. No other count in the article changes: both guidance experiments affirm equivalence at 5 points, and three of the five information experiments affirm it at 10 points, under either standard error."),

stopifnot(nrow(entries) == max(entries$entry), !anyDuplicated(entries$entry),
          all(is.na(entries$corrected) == (entries$form == "note")),
          identical(entries$entry[entries$form == "note"], c(11, 32, 44, 45)))

# Gate: corrected_values agrees with the sentence it was glued into ----
# The column and the sentence are written from one object, so they begin in agreement and
# this gate exists for the edit that separates them: a value moved from one marked span to
# another, a span reworded to carry a second number, a claim id appended without its value.
# Each value has to be inside the span it belongs to, matched by position where the counts
# line up, and inside SOME span where an entry marks a label as well as a number and its
# spans outnumber its values. A count the sentence spells out is accepted in its spelled form.
marked_spans <- function(x) str_match_all(x, "\\[\\[(.*?)\\]\\]")[[1]][, 2]

in_span <- function(v, s) {
  s <- str_remove_all(s, ",")
  str_detect(s, fixed(v)) ||
    (str_detect(v, "^[0-9]+$") && as.integer(v) %in% seq_len(25) &&
       str_detect(s, fixed(spell(as.integer(v)))))
}

quantified <- entries |>
  filter(!is.na(corrected_values)) |>
  mutate(ids = str_split(claim_ids, ";"), values = str_split(corrected_values, ";"),
         spans = map(corrected, marked_spans))

stopifnot(all(lengths(quantified$ids) == lengths(quantified$values)))

value_placed <- pmap_lgl(quantified, function(...) {
  e <- list(...)
  if (length(e$values) == length(e$spans)) {
    all(map2_lgl(e$values, e$spans, in_span))
  } else {
    all(map_lgl(e$values, \(v) any(map_lgl(e$spans, \(s) in_span(v, s)))))
  }
})

if (!all(value_placed)) {
  print(quantified |> filter(!value_placed) |> select(entry, title, corrected_values, corrected))
  stop("An entry's corrected_values are not in the spans of its corrected sentence.")
}

# An entry that changes a quantity has to say which one, and an entry that changes none may
# not carry a value. The class is the declaration and this is where it binds. A note-form
# entry corrects nothing and carries NA even where its class is quantity, and an entry with
# no claim_ids has no claim to carry a value for.
has_ids <- !is.na(entries$claim_ids) & entries$claim_ids != ""
# Entries whose claim id names something no corrected token states as a number carry NA by
# name, and the list is the only exemption.
no_numeric_claim <- 2
stopifnot(
  all(!is.na(entries$corrected_values[entries$class == "quantity" & entries$form != "note" &
                                        has_ids & !entries$entry %in% no_numeric_claim])),
  all(is.na(entries$corrected_values[entries$class != "quantity"])),
  all(is.na(entries$corrected_values[entries$form == "note"])),
  all(is.na(entries$corrected_values) | has_ids)
)

# The spine's markup, resolved for this document. Another renderer resolves it differently.
bold <- function(x) str_replace_all(str_replace_all(x, fixed("*"), "\\*"), "\\[\\[(.*?)\\]\\]", "**\\1**")

# A heading is only a heading when a blank line precedes it, which is why every emitted
# entry opens with one.
emit_entry <- function(n) {
  e <- entries |> filter(entry == n)
  cat("\n\n## ", e$entry, ". ", e$title, "\n\nPublished, ",
      str_remove(e$location, "^published "), ":\n\n> ", bold(e$published), sep = "")
  if (e$form != "note") cat("\n\nCorrected:\n\n> ", bold(e$corrected), sep = "")
  if (nzchar(e$note)) cat("\n\n", e$note, sep = "")
  cat("\n")
}

sections <- list(
  article = c(1, 2, 5:12, 15:19, 21:28, 41, 45, 46),
  references = 29:32,
  appendix = c(3, 4, 13, 14, 20, 33:40, 42, 43, 44, 47)
)
stopifnot(setequal(unlist(sections), entries$entry), !anyDuplicated(unlist(sections)))
n_corrections <- sum(entries$form != "note")
n_notes <- sum(entries$form == "note")
```

This note lists `r n_corrections` corrections, and `r spell(n_notes)` items it flags without correcting, in "Endorsements vs. information: experimental evidence of backlash and parallel persuasion during the COVID-19 public health crisis," published in *PNAS Nexus* 4(6):pgaf185, doi [10.1093/pnasnexus/pgaf185](https://doi.org/10.1093/pnasnexus/pgaf185), and its online appendix. **Two of the corrections concern claims the article makes.** On p. 4 the article says that the sign and significance of the interaction terms match those of the differences-in-CATEs in all cases but one, and that equivalence can be affirmed at 10 points in two of the four mandate vignettes. By the printed estimates the first count is four, not one (entry 21), and under the correct standard error for the difference the second is one, not two (entry 22), because the deposit's code mistypes that standard error. Two more concern what a printed figure and an appendix table show: the series labels of Fig. 2 are swapped (entry 46), and the G-1 and G-3 rows of the appendix's guidance equivalence table carry each other's numbers (entry 47). No estimate in the article's main tables or figures changes value. The appendix's equivalence tables print standard errors and equivalence p-values from the mistyped formula, and they are not reprinted here.

Four corrections are counts of respondents or arms: the headline number of respondents and the size of survey wave five (entries 1 and 2), the number of estimates in the appendix's comparison of weighted and unweighted models (entry 4), and one arm of a CONSORT diagram (entry 20). The rest are descriptions of stimuli, samples, and outcomes that do not match the appendix, labels and captions, cross-references to appendix figures and tables, wording and spelling in the article and the appendix, and details of the reference list. The `r spell(n_notes)` items without a correction are cases where the page or the deposit cannot say what the right value is, or where a repair would rewrite the authors' sentence (entries 11, 32, 44, and 45).

All were found by reading the article and its appendix word by word, together with the maintained replication, which recomputes every number the article prints from the deposited replication archive ([osf.io/bwv3c](https://osf.io/bwv3c/)) and checks each against the printed value. Each quotation was checked against an image of the published page, and the references were checked against the Crossref record named in each entry's note. The counts in entries 1 and 22 are computed from the maintained output at the time this document is rendered. The code supporting the maintained analysis is at [github.com/active-maintenance-aec/baxter-king_etal_2025](https://github.com/active-maintenance-aec/baxter-king_etal_2025).

# The article

```{r article-entries, results="asis"}
walk(sections$article, emit_entry)
```

# The article's references

```{r reference-entries, results="asis"}
walk(sections$references, emit_entry)
```

# The appendix

```{r appendix-entries, results="asis"}
walk(sections$appendix, emit_entry)
```

```{r emit-spine}
# The machine-readable spine, written wherever this document is rendered. Anything else
# that needs these entries reads it rather than keeping its own copy, so the two cannot
# drift.
write_csv(entries, here("errata_entries.csv"))
```
